title: The Time Machine
author: H. G. Wells
ru: Изобретатель путешествует в далёкое будущее и встречает элоев и морлоков

chapters.title: Chapter 1. The Fourth Dimension
chapters.text:
The Time Traveller, as I shall call him, was explaining a difficult idea to us. His grey eyes were shining, and his usually pale face was red with excitement. We were sitting by the fire after dinner in his house in Richmond.

There were several of us that evening: a doctor, a psychologist, a provincial mayor, a very young man called Filby, and myself.

“You must listen carefully,” he said. “Everything around us has length, width and height. But there is a fourth dimension too, and that is Time.”

“But we cannot move in Time,” said the psychologist. “We can go up and down, left and right, but not backwards or forwards in Time.”

“That is where you are wrong,” said the Time Traveller. “When I remember something very clearly, I go back in time in my mind for a moment. And a balloon can go up against gravity. Why should we not go against Time too? I have been working on this for years, and I have built a machine.”

We all laughed, but he went to his workshop and came back with a small, shining object, not much bigger than a clock. It was made of metal, ivory and crystal, and it was very beautifully made.

“This is a model of my Time Machine,” he said. He put it on a small table near the fire. “This little lever sends it into the future, and this one into the past. Look carefully, because I do not want you to think it is a trick.”

He asked the psychologist to press the lever with his own finger. There was a breath of wind, and the lamp flame jumped. The model turned round, became unclear like a ghost for a second, and was gone. Only the lamp was left on the table.

Everyone was silent for a minute. Then the doctor said, “Are you serious? Do you really believe that the machine has travelled into Time?”

“Certainly,” answered the Time Traveller. “And I have a big machine nearly finished in my laboratory. I intend to take a journey on it myself.”

He took us to the laboratory, and there we saw a larger copy of the little machine, with a seat for a man. Some parts were not finished yet.

We did not believe him, of course. We thought it was a clever trick. But none of us could explain how he had done it.

chapters.title: Chapter 2. The Traveller Returns
chapters.text:
The next Thursday I went again to Richmond. When I arrived, four or five men were already in the dining room, but our host was not there. The doctor showed me a note. It said that the Time Traveller was late and that we should start dinner without him.

We had just begun to eat when the door opened slowly. Our host stood there, and we all looked at him in shock. His clothes were dusty and dirty, and his sleeves were green. His hair was grey, with more grey in it than before. His face was very pale, and there was a half-healed cut on his chin. He limped as he walked, and he looked exhausted, as if he had suffered terribly.

He smiled weakly and drank a glass of wine in one go.

“I am starving,” he said. “Give me some meat. I have not eaten meat for eight days. I will tell you everything, but first I must wash and change. I will be back in a few minutes.”

When he had gone, we all began to talk at once. Was he ill? Had he had an accident?

He came back, ate a lot of mutton with enormous appetite, and then led us into the smoking room.

“I will tell you the whole story,” he said, “but you must not interrupt me. It will sound like lies, but it is true. At four o’clock this afternoon I was in my laboratory, and since then I have lived eight days, days that no human being has ever lived before.”

He began. “Last Thursday I showed some of you the model. Today I finished the real machine. At ten o’clock this morning I sat in the seat, took the starting lever in one hand and the stopping lever in the other, and pressed the first one.

“I felt as if I was falling. I looked round and saw the laboratory exactly as before. Then I looked at the clock. A moment ago it had said a minute or so past ten. Now it was nearly half past three!

“I pushed the lever further. Night came like the turning off of a lamp, and in another moment came tomorrow. I saw great buildings rise and fall like dreams.

“I was travelling faster and faster, and I began to feel afraid. At last I pulled the stopping lever too quickly. The machine fell over, and I was thrown through the air. When I looked up, I was sitting on soft grass in a heavy storm of hail. The little dials said that it was the year 802,701.”

chapters.title: Chapter 3. The Eloi
chapters.text:
“When the hail stopped, I looked around me,” the Time Traveller continued. “Near me there was a huge white statue of a sphinx with wings. Beyond it I saw great palaces among green trees and flowers. The whole world looked like a beautiful garden.

“Then I saw some people coming towards me. They were small, about four feet tall, and they wore bright, soft clothes. They were very beautiful, but they looked weak, like children. One of them came right up to me and laughed. He was not afraid of me at all. They touched my hands and my clothes gently, to see if I was real.

“They spoke a sweet language that I could not understand. I pointed to the sun and made the sound of thunder. They understood that I had come from the sky, and they were delighted. They put flowers around my neck and took me into one of the great buildings.

“Inside, it was a huge hall with dirty, broken windows. Hundreds of these people were sitting on cushions, eating fruit. They ate no meat at all. I learned later that they called themselves the Eloi.

“I tried to learn their language, but it was hard. They had very short attention and got tired quickly, like small children. They did no work. They did not study. They only played, swam, ate fruit and slept. There were no old people and no sick people among them.

“At first I thought I understood this world. Science had won the fight against nature. There was no more danger, no disease and no need to work. So mankind had become weak, gentle and lazy. Strength and intelligence are born from need and danger. Without them, people lose them. I thought it was the sunset of mankind.

“But I was wrong, as you will hear.

“That evening I went back to the place where I had left my machine. It was gone! I felt a terrible fear. Without it I would be a prisoner in this strange world forever. I ran round like a madman, screaming.

“The next morning I studied the ground calmly. I saw a line in the grass. Somebody had dragged the machine into the base of the sphinx statue. There were bronze doors in the base, but they were closed, and I could not open them. When I asked the Eloi about the doors, they looked strangely unhappy and turned away.

“I understood that I must be patient. Nobody could use the machine without the levers, and I had them in my pocket. I decided to learn more about this world, and one day find a way through those doors.”

chapters.title: Chapter 4. Weena and the Wells
chapters.text:
“A few days later I saw some of the Eloi swimming in the river,” the Time Traveller went on. “Suddenly one of them, a small girl, was caught by the current and began to drown. The strange thing was that nobody tried to help her. I jumped into the water and pulled her out.

“Her name was Weena, and after that she followed me everywhere like a child. She brought me flowers and cried when I left her. I grew very fond of her. From her I learned something important. She was terribly afraid of the dark. All the Eloi were. At night they never went out, and they always slept together in large groups.

“One early morning, in the grey light, I saw some white, ape-like figures running across the hill. I told myself that they were ghosts, or that I was imagining things. But a few days later, in a dark room of one of the ruins, I saw two large eyes shining at me. I reached out my hand and touched something soft. The creature ran away. It was small and pale, like a white ape, with large grey-red eyes and light hair on its head and back. It ran to a round hole in the ground and climbed down into the darkness.

“I had seen many of these holes before. They were like deep wells, with a tower over each one. Now I understood. There was a second race of people, living under the ground.

“The Eloi called them the Morlocks. The Morlocks could not bear the light, and they came up only at night.

“Slowly I began to understand the truth. In my own time, the rich people lived in beautiful houses, and the workers spent their lives in dark factories. Over thousands of years this difference had grown until the two groups had become two different species. The rich had become the Eloi, beautiful and useless. The workers had become the Morlocks, living underground with their machines.

“But I was still wrong. I did not yet know the most horrible part.

“I was sure that the Morlocks had taken my Time Machine. So one day I decided to go down one of the wells. Weena cried, but I began to climb down the metal hooks in the wall.

“At the bottom it was completely dark. I heard machines working, and felt soft, cold hands touching me. I had only a few matches. When I lit one, they ran away from the light. By its light I saw a piece of red meat on a table. I felt sick, and suddenly I understood what the Morlocks ate.”

chapters.title: Chapter 5. The Night in the Forest
chapters.text:
“I climbed up out of the well as fast as I could,” the Time Traveller said. “The Morlocks followed me and pulled at my feet, but I kicked them away. When I came up into the light, I lay on the ground and shook with horror.

“Now I understood the whole terrible truth. The Eloi were not the masters, and the Morlocks were not their servants. The Morlocks fed and clothed the Eloi, but only in the way a farmer feeds his cattle. At night, they came up and took the Eloi as food. That was why the Eloi feared the darkness.

“I needed a weapon, and I needed a safe place to sleep. In the distance I had seen a great green building. I decided to go there with Weena.

“The building was an enormous old museum, the Palace of Green Porcelain. In one hall there was a library, but all the books had turned to dust long ago. But I found two useful things: a heavy iron bar from an old machine, and a box of matches that still worked. I also found some camphor, which burns well.

“It was late when we left the museum, and we had to cross a thick forest. Night fell quickly. Weena was tired, so I carried her. Soon I heard soft footsteps around us, and I felt small hands touching my coat. The Morlocks had come.

“I lit a fire to keep them away, and it worked for a while. But I was so tired that I fell asleep. When I woke up, the fire was out, and the Morlocks were all over me. Weena had been taken from my arms. I fought like a wild animal with my iron bar and felt their bones break.

“Then I saw a strange red light among the trees. My first fire had spread through the dry forest, and now the whole wood was burning. The Morlocks ran blindly towards the flames, because the light made them helpless. I ran with them, and I killed several of them with my bar. But I could not find Weena anywhere.

“I spent the rest of that terrible night on a small hill in the middle of the burning forest. In the morning I searched among the ashes, but there was no sign of her. I think the Morlocks had taken her, or that she had died in the fire. I shall never know.

“I felt great sadness and loneliness. Weena had been my only friend in that strange world. At last, tired and burned, I walked back to the white sphinx. I had only one idea now: to find my machine and go home.”

chapters.title: Chapter 6. The End of the World
chapters.text:
“When I came to the white sphinx,” the Time Traveller continued, “the bronze doors were open. Inside, in a small room, stood my Time Machine. I was sure that it was a trap, but I did not care.

“At once the doors closed behind me with a crash. I was in total darkness. I tried to light a match, but these were safety matches that only lit on the box, and I had left the box outside. Their hands were on me. I fought them off, fixed the levers in place, jumped into the seat and pulled the lever. The darkness disappeared, and I was travelling through Time again.

“In my excitement I did not look at the dials. When I did, I saw that I was going forward, not back. I was travelling further and further into the future, millions of years.

“At last I stopped. I was on a lonely beach. The sun was huge, red and still, low in the sky. The earth had stopped turning. The air was very thin and cold. There were no people, no animals and no flowers. Then I saw a huge crab moving towards me, and I went further.

“Thirty million years later I stopped for the last time. The sun had grown even bigger and darker. Snow was falling, and there was a terrible silence. All life had nearly ended. I saw only a round black thing with long arms, jumping in the red water. So I turned the machine around and travelled home.

“Then I saw the walls of my own laboratory appear around me. Then I came into this room and saw you all at dinner.”

He looked at us for a long time. “I know that you cannot believe me,” he said. “Take it as a story, if you like.”

The others smiled politely and went home. But the next day I came back. The Time Traveller had a small camera in his hand.

“I am going on another journey,” he said. “I shall bring back photographs and proof. Wait for me for half an hour.”

I heard the sound of the machine and ran to the laboratory. There was a breath of wind and a crash of glass. The room was empty. The Time Traveller had gone.

That was three years ago. He has never come back. And when I think of him, I remember two strange white flowers that he brought home from the future. Weena had put them into his pocket. They show that even when strength and intelligence had gone, gratitude and tenderness still lived on in the heart of man.
